assessments.assessment: Classical equilibrium ideal-gas assumptions, fixed amount, absent bulk flow and excluded electronic excitation are explicit. Neglecting interaction potential is a model/zero-point convention, not a universal statement about real gases. Total gas mass is distinguished from particle mass. Multiplying mean atomic energy by particle count gives the original(3-20); absolute temperature and the limited active-degree-of-freedom range for more complex gases are correctly qualified.

For fixed-quantity ideal gas, isothermal internal-energy change is zero. With only heat and volume work, A' is gas-on-surroundings work and equals signed Q. Adiabatic Delta U=A uses external-on-gas work: compression heats, while expansion cools only when the gas does outward work. No claim that free expansion must cool, that rapid means adiabatic, or that positive heat is required for every isothermal path.

Sealed lamp mass and volume, hence mass density, are held approximately fixed. Pressure relation determines RMS speed, not arithmetic mean speed; the source overline-v formulas are retained with an explicit local RMS interpretation.

The complete original solution is explicitly a fixed-amount, constant-volume gas approximation, not the generic behavior of a flexible balloon. Boundary work vanishes; heat equals monatomic internal-energy increase. p and V in the substitution are initial-state data, the denominator is absolute initial temperature, and temperature difference has the same numerical value in kelvins and Celsius degrees. Gas-only scope excludes balloon heating and expansion work.

Source references, formulas and both full printed solutions retained as prose, with no invented written tasks. Avogadro, Mendeleev and Clapeyron mentions have individual source-bound historical_entities declarations. Amount times R times absolute temperature has energy units; pressure divided by density has speed-squared units, and pV times the temperature ratio has energy units.

Surface evaporation and bulk boiling are distinguished qualitatively. Escape requires suitable energy/local interactions, not every escaping molecule being far faster than the mean. Vapor is gas, while visible liquid cloud droplets are distinguished from gaseous water. Source examples and the prior-grade reference remain, without invented personal experience or a hot-water experimental instruction.

Same-temperature vaporization is not modeled as ordinary temperature rise or solely increased particle speed. Changed intermolecular interaction energy and possible expansion against external pressure are both retained; heat is not incorrectly equated to translational kinetic-energy increase or solely to internal-energy change when expansion work is present. Specific latent heat is per unit mass, with substance, temperature and corresponding pressure/phase conditions specified.

assessments.assessment: All original water values and comparison fractions remain expressly attributed to the book as approximate trend/quantity examples, not certified contemporary precision property data. The named-liquid range is not presented as universal, and mixture limitations are explicit. Changing saturation/coexistence pressure is identified across temperatures; the text does not imply liquid-vapor equilibrium at one atmosphere for every listed temperature. The molecular explanation of decreasing latent heat is qualitative, not a literal breaking of attraction forces.
